FOREWORD

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 15 December 1980, after the draft finalized by the Cotton and Cotton Products Sectional Committee, had been approved by the Textile Division Council. 0.2 This standard, which was orginally published in 1969, has been taken up for revision in the light of the experience gained during the use over the period. 0.3 Cotton yarn waste, a bye-product of cotton spinning industry, is used for cleaning machines and instruments. After hand picking the hard and twisted threads, loops, metallic wires, lags, etc the waste yarn is teased adequately to open out the lumps and to remove embedded impurities like dirt, grit, etc. 0.4 To ~familiarize the industry with Units ), the recommended SL Units given in Appendix B. 0.4.1 Standards of SI Units. of weights International system for use in the textile of units industry ( SI are use

and Measures

Act, 1976, also stipulates

0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, ~observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded of in accordance with IS: 2-1960*. The significant places retaines in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 1. SCOPE 1.1 This standard cotton yarn waste. prescribes the requirements of two types of teased

3. GENERAL

It should 3.1 The cntton yarn waste should be well teased and blended. be reasonably free from non-textile substances like dirt, grit, wooden chips, bidi ends, papers, feathers, etc and also free from textile impurities such as soft waste ( loose untwisted strands ), hard twisted, folded or sized yarn, rags, etc. 3.2 The cotton yarn waste shall be free from loading matter barvtes, china clay, etc. It shall not look oily or dirty and appearance and free from lumps. such as lime, have a clear

3.3 The cotton yarn waste shall consist substantially of absorbent cotton yarns. Staple fibre yarn ( viscose rayon ) up to 20 percent may be perTraces of man-made fibres yarn other mitted, if not stated otherwise. than staple yarn are also permissible. 4. 4.2 Sealed Sample - The supply shall be in conformity with the sample, agreed between buyer and seller and sealed accordingly, in respect of indeterminable characteristics like general appearance, shade etc. 5. PACKING 5.1 Cotton yarn waste shall be packed in bales having net mass of 25 or The cotton yarn waste shall be lightly pressedto form 50 kg as agreed. a rectangular and wrapped with an inner layer of polyethylene film ( see IS : 2508-1977*) of 40 microns thickness, minimum or alternatively kraft paper ( see IS : 1397-1967t ) waterproof paper ( see IS : 1398-1968$) and an outer layer of heavy tee cloth (see IS: 3751-1966s ) or equivalent *Specification for low density

hessian. The overlapping of the packing materials shall be at least 10 cm so as to ensure full protection to the contents of the bale. The overlapping of the outer layer of hessian shall be such that it could be properly and securely sewn round the'bale. The bale shall Be stitched with double 3-ply jute twine with not less than 6 stitches per dm taking care not to pierce the inner layer of the bale during stitching. Sufficient hessian shall be pulled out at each corner to form ears-of about 15 cm in length. The bale shall be stripped with at least 2 bailing hoops to ensure safety and prevent pilferage of the contents during transit/storage. The bales shall not be press-packed.

APPENDIX ( Tuble 1 )
METHODS A-l. DIRT, GRIT, ETC OF TEST

A

A-l.1 Take cotton yarn waste about 100 g from portions of composite Spread the sample uniformly sample and determine its mass accurately. in a 1.70 mm IS Sieve [ see IS : 460( Part I )-1978* 1. Open the sieve on Open out the the ground or table suitably covered with a white paper. sample thoroughly inside the sieve, care being taken to see that while opening no fibre falls out of the sieve. Lift the sieve and shake it horizontally 50 times, taking care that dirt, grit, etc, from the sieve falls on the white paper only, After 50 shakes, collect the dirt, grit, etc, from Express the dirt, grit, etc, the paper and determine its mass accurately. as percentage of the mass of the sample. A-2. TEXTILE/NON-TEXTILE IMPURITIES A-2.1 Take cotton waste about 2 kg from portions of composite sample and determine its mass accurately. Spread the sample on a clean table Determine and segregate the textile/non-textile impurities manually. their mass separately and ~express them as percentage of the mass of the sample. A-3. SOFT WASTE

A-3.1 After opening out and shaking the sample for removing dirt, grit, etc ( SEC A-l ), determine the mass of clean sample. Segrrgate the soft waste, flutty material manually. Determine its mnss accurately and express it as a percentage of the mass of the clean sample.
*Specification for test sieves: Part I Wire cloth test sieves.

7

IS : 5485 - 1980 A-4. COLOURED YARN

A-4.1 After opening out and shaking the sample for removing dirt,' grit, etc ( see A-l ), determine the mass of clean sample. Segregate the coloured yarn waste manually and determine its mass accurately. Express it as percentage of mass of the clean sample.
